In this work it will be shown how an intelligent gripper can be controlled with the help of low-cost components in order to recognize objects independently and lift them safely with adapted gripping force.

articleTitle: The Use of CT- Scan with 3- D Reconstruction for Planning Surgery In Children with Tibia Plateau Fractures
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This study was aimed to assess the opportunity of using CT scan exam with 3-D reconstruction in children with tibia plateau fractures. This type of fracture occurs rarely in the paediatric population, generally in older children, either as isolated lesion or part of multiple trauma. Appropriate radiology diagnosis is required for classifying the fracture according to Schatzker's criteria and deciding the treatment plan. There are still controversies in the literature regarding the use of CT scan examination as part of the diagnosis protocol. We present two cases of children with knee trauma in which the standard X-Ray exam was equivocal in identifying the type of tibia plateau fracture. Detailed view of fracture anatomy was obtained by using CT-Scan exam with 3-D reconstruction. Surgery was performed in accordance with these data, and the outcome was favourable in both cases. We consider that CT-Scan with 3-D reconstruction is useful for planning surgery in children with tibia plateau fractures. This examination protocol should be routinely used in such difficult cases.

articleTitle: Operation Characteristics of Low Power Asynchronous Motors Supplied by Static Converters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the paper there is carried out a thorough study of drives with asynchronous motors supplied by voltage and frequency static converters. A lot of simulations are presented, emphasizing the distorting regime effects, both in the supply network and in the asynchronous motor. The mathematical model used makes also possible an energetic balance sheet. The results and simulations carried out consider the magnetic saturation on the path of the main and leakage field of the slots. The researches carried out with an asynchronous motor rated at 1.5 kW, supplied by a static converter have emphasized that the errors do not exceed 2.2% between the simulated quantities and the quantities determined experimentally. These results justify the research carried out, which provides correct qualitative and quantitative simulations for the steady state.

articleTitle: Parameters Affecting the Resistance of Earth Grounding Installation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Grounding installations are essential for the human safety but also for the normal operation of the electrical installation. Its design is difficult because the dependence on different and divers parameters. The paper presents a study regarding the importance of thickness, diameter, length, type of used material and arrangement in getting the smallest resistance possible in a grounding installation, while using the minimum amount of material.

articleTitle: Analysis of Light Design in the Lighting Laboratory of the Riga Technical University
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Given the fact that it is required to increase the efficiency of energy consumption in the premises, it is necessary to develop an effective lighting design that can be used both in old buildings and in new projects. To achieve a lower overall energy consumption by a building without sacrificing the quality of lighting, effective lighting modeling is needed, which allows to obtain reliable results for models as close as possible to real life, taking into account energy-saving lighting devices, integration of daylight in order to reduce energy consumption and maintenance costs, etc.The research evaluates possibility to measure luminance of light sources and detect sources of glare, using ordinary digital single-lens reflex camera (DSLR) and image editing software. Methodology and workflow is presented. The results then are discussed and ways to improve the accuracy of the measurements are highlighted.

articleTitle: Educational Resource for Wind Turbine Behaviour Assessment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Renewable energy resources are and will be increasingly used, both due to classical resources depletion and due to the recent climate changes. The aim of the paper is to present modern tools for studying the behaviour of doubly fed induction generator wind turbine in order to synchronize with the grid. In the ENERED laboratory, can be implemented different configurations of wind turbines and may be simulated study cases for grid connection and integration of wind farm. The relationship between the rotor current and the stator voltage, as well as the influence of speed and current on stator voltage are highlighted in laboratory simulation. To generate testing signals, power system processes records and simulation software are used. For education purposes a test model, suitable for wind turbine is created.

articleTitle: Susceptor Assisted Microwave Processing of Polymers for Adhesive Production
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Microwave activated adhesives were manufactured, at laboratory scale, with micro-nanosized fillers embedded in traditional thermoplastic matrix. These metal-based susceptors are highly loss materials (e.g.: iron and aluminium micro/nano-powders), which rapidly heat-up by means of the microwaves/radio frequency irradiation. The heat is then transferred to the matrix through conventional heat transfer. This is a very effective technology to create reversible adhesives suitable for many applications in various industries including the automotive and the aerospace industry. Susceptor technology is a good way to replace traditional hot-melt adhesives. Hot-melt adhesives are thermoplastic bonding materials applied as melts that achieve a solid state and resultant strength on cooling. These thermoplastics of 100% solid materials melt in the temperature range from 65 °C to 180 °C. Theoretically, any thermoplastic can be a hot-melt adhesive, however, preferred materials are usually solid up to 79.4 °C or higher. Metal particles are suitable for susceptor materials that create hysteresis heating-based Curie temperature control for polymer processing. The electrical properties of the reinforcement are mainly used for matrix melting by induction heating. Induction heating has several features, including high efficiency and economic benefits and environmental benefits. In this study we investigated a formulation of MW/activated adhesives made of LDPE mixed with aluminium micro-particles. An optimization of the best materials concentration and dimensions was carried out according with the electro-magnetic performances evaluated.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition Expressed Contextually for Romanian Language
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper describes the results obtained by using emotional speech database contextually expressed in theater plays. The emotions analyzed in this study are happiness, sadness, anger and neutral tone. The best recognition was 73.67% and it was obtained for the hybrid feature vectors which include cepstral coefficients: PARCOR (partial correlation coef.) + LAR (log area ratio coef.) + AC (autocorrelation coef).

articleTitle: Virtual Prototyping in Telecommunications. Issues and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: For the last several years the frequency in telecommunications increased over GHz range. Such frequencies came with side effects such as crosstalk, overshot, undershoot, timing issues. The designing process had to implement new ideas, parts, components and processing capabilities. The DDR (double data-rate) memories are used extensively. The latest families, DDR3, DDR4 pushed the technological boundaries to the point where the hardware and software work together to keep under control the high-speed issues mentioned above. The most important thing is that the human must be assisted by the machine to settle the constraints the projects should comply with to fulfill the requirements. Specialized tools have been developed to improve the equipment quality, the time to market and the redesigning process. Mentor Graphics HyperLynx, with both approaches (pre and post layout) is the solution we propose to solve the DDR timing issues. In the current paper, the DDR memory analysis tool's capability and results are presented. The wizard assisting the designer, the power of calculation and the results confirm the value of HyperLynx solution developed by the Mentor Graphics company, in virtual prototyping.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of Tankless Heating System Using PLC
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article presents a thermal analysis of a tankless heating system based on programmable logic controller (PLC) which is used to acquire and process the thermal data provided by a suitable temperature transducer. The temperature variation has been recorded during transient and steady-state conditions. The thermal analysis has been performed at different water flow and also for different thermal power. The power consumption of the tank less heating system can be decreased using an automation system based on micro controller and PLC in the case of industrial applications.

articleTitle: Cloud Platform for Medical Data Acquisition and Physician-Patient Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents an open web platform (EMIM) which implements multiple functionalities for the health sector: medical data storage, physician-patient dialogue, online appointments, medical history, self-management disease and other. There are many other applications which integrate some of these services, but this platform is designed to integrate all these into one unique cloud database. In this way, no medical data are lost anymore in various isolated computers, in this application once the data are uploaded, then those data are accessible anytime, anywhere.

articleTitle: Experimental model for measuring the currents in the rotor cage bars of an induction machine
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to develop an experimental model able to measure the currents in rotor cage bars of an induction machine. In order to achieve it, the authors propose a reversed machine mathematical model, in which the machine rotor represents the inductor and the armature becomes the stator.

Author Keywords: equivalent magnetic circuit method (EMCM) reversed model

articleTitle: A Cost Effective Boost Converter for a Hybrid Low- Voltage Neighbourhood Network
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The scope of this paper is to present a highly controllable and low-cost implementation of a boost converter which can be integrated in an AC and DC hybrid low-voltage network to be used in future distribution architectures. The proposed solution is tasked with enhancing the efficiency of the used energy in a prosumer oriented paradigm consisting of AC and DC connected users having loads, local production and storage, by unleashing energy resilience and immunity at prosumer level. Moreover, the boost converter solution avoids a vendor-locked architecture and enables different energy strategies for the emerging clusters of prosumers using both legacy AC and emerging DC connectivity.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Spatial-Temporal Variability of the Near Field Components in the Proximity of a TETRA Portable Terminal
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper is focused on the electromagnetic exposure assessment in the proximity of a Terrestrial Trunked Radio (TETRA) terminal. For the first time distinct measurements of the electric field component (E) and of the magnetic field component (H) are presented in the distance range 8-20 cm. The results show that the E-field component has a greater prevalence on the exposure. Maximum values of 100% for E, and 17% for H component respectively were encountered in the near field of the terminal, if compared to the occupational limits given in the ICNIRP protective guidelines.

articleTitle: Video Coordination System for Textile Manufacturing Process
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Global textile industry along with other industries is in full recession. To withstand and grow in an increasingly competitive market, textile companies must comply with the market demands through the fast fashion react concept, namely the production of small quantities of products with a high degree of difficulty and high added value. Moreover product quality certification is a first priority. Thus, the producers must be able to demonstrate they have a quality assurance system for the manufacturing processes. Considering the fact that labor costs increase significantly, it is necessary to implement automated systems for the manufacturing processes, allowing replacement of human operators and thus increasing the productivity and product quality along with reducing the time needed for the production workflow to adapt to new models.

articleTitle: Temperature influence in Direct Green 26 dye degradation rate with non-thermal plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The present paper aims to study the effect of non-thermal plasma treatment on the aqueous solutions emphasizing the discolouring process. There were investigated the influences of solution flow rate for the same voltage applied to the surface gliding discharges reactor. The paper presents the influence of temperature on pollutant decolorization. The non-thermal plasma technology decreases the organic pollutants from aqueous solutions. The objective of this work was to develop new reactor configurations to enhance liquid phase treatment and to assess dye degradation in surface gliding arc reactors.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Reactive Species Produced in Water by GlidArc Plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The goal of the paper is to study the influence of non-thermal plasma (NPT) generated by a GlidArc discharge H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> formation in water. The paper presents a preliminary study of the influence of plasma activated water (PAW) on plant growth. The influence of gas and water flow rates on reactive species produced in PAW has been followed.

articleTitle: Wideband Three-axis Magnetic Field Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband three-axis magnetic field sensor operating in the frequency range from 50 Hz to 100 kHz is presented. It consists of a three-axis coil probe connected to an analog processing circuit, which is able to accurately reconstruct the waveforms of the three orthogonal components of the incident magnetic flux density. The sensor can be used in conjunction with common measuring equipment, such as a digital oscilloscope, but highest performance is obtained if used in conjunction with a data acquisition device and dedicated measurement software. The sensor features flat frequency response and high dynamic range, and can be used for both human exposure assessments and electromagnetic compatibility applications.

articleTitle: Testing Equipment for DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: For the automotive industry and various electric drives the use of the DC motor in different operating modes is very important. Due to the very large constructive variety of the DC motors, a highly versatile power supply circuit was designed in this article. The best price-performance ratio has been pursued. The most efficient way to adjust the operating mode of the DC motor is, by far, the Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) control. Several configurations with different admissible intervals for different voltages and currents have been studied. For testing, two different shape and performance electric motors were used. One electric motor has a rotor winding in the magnetic field generated by a permanent magnet (voltage 60V and 1000 rpm) while the second DC motor has both coils winding (voltage 230V and 14000 rpm). The stand was built in accordance with the current regulations on safety in operation and with the restriction of hazardous substances compliance on technology.

articleTitle: In House Development and Testing of Nanostructured Inks for Inkjet Printed Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The growth of population has led to environmental pollution due to the desire of most part of people to have a higher living standard. The term environmental pollution means the penetration of liquid, solid and gaseous substances and electric, thermal, sonic and magnetic energy into the environment, in amounts that cause the change of composition and quality of natural components with an undesirable impact on humans, fauna, and flora. This is why nowadays, the prevention of environmental pollution by using nanotechnologies to reduce waste quantities is so important. Nanomaterials can be found in diverse applications of environmental issues. The main advantage of nanomaterials is that they can be controlled in order to create new properties that are not available in the particles made from the same material on a macro or micrometric scale. Other features of nanomaterials refer to an increased reactivity and a modified reaction rate, properties that determine the nanomaterials to have an increased contact with contaminating agents, leading to a rapid reduction of their concentrations. Some of the applications of nano-sized materials are still in the research phase. At present, studies regarding particles such as carbon nanotubes, dendrimers, self-assembled monolayers TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> on porous and organically modified silica(SOMS) substrates are conducted.Some important nanomaterials are: Metallic oxides containing zinc oxide (ZnO), titanium dioxide (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), iron oxide (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>), cerium oxide (CeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) Carbon nanotubes and fullerenes in the form of ellipsoidal flakes or carbon nanotubes and spheroidal flakes. Zero-valent metals including zero-valent iron with an increased surface reactivity used in soil, water and sediment remediation processes. Quantum dots are semiconductors with linked electron-gap pairs available in all the three dimensions of the space. Dendrimers are polymers with a high degree of branching, created in order to include different functional groups. Composite nanomaterials made from nanomaterial material combined with a massive material or 2 or more nanoscale materials.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Renewable Energy Sector's Development Impact on the CO2 Emissions in Romania
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Fossil fuels burning is one of the main techniques utilized in order to generate electricity in large scale power plants. However, in the last decades, due to growing concern related to the impact of toxic gases, solid particles and greenhouse gases associated with fossil fuels burning on the environment, significant measures were considered in order to reduce these negative consequences. Along these measures, the development of the renewable energies was considered a key factor, and consequently was encouraged through several political decisions. Romania, as a European Union's member had to implement the established directives and, consequently, the renewable energy sector known a rapid evolution in the past eight years. In this paper an analysis is conducted in order to evaluate the impact of the renewable energy sector development on the CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions levels in Romania.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method for Studyingthe Motion Graphs optimization in Electric Drive Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper intends to propose a solution for the transient regime study at asynchronous motor, using a PLC control. The solution allows adjusting the acceleration, the deceleration, the speed, the jerk (mechanical shock) and monitoring the jerk during the start and stop regime of the motor with a pendulum. The pendulum is moved using a ball screw and nut assembly with an induction motor, which is controlled with a high performance modular drive system-Sinamics S120, from Siemens. The S120 drive has Profinet communication and is connected in an industrial network with a PLC (S7-1516) and an HMI (KTP700).

articleTitle: Design and Use of the Callflow Module in Executable Choreographies for IoT
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is an ecosystem of computer devices, people or animals which hold unique identifiers and have the ability to transfer data over the network without involving human-to-human or human-to-computer interaction. Over the years, there have been a number of challenges in building a scalable IoT system. These challenges include asynchronous communication, for which we propose a solution developed within the PrivateSky project [1], based on the representation of the asynchronous code as a set of phases in a workflow, which we will present in Section 4.

articleTitle: New Techniques Used to Implement Transformation Stations and Protection Functions in Transformation Stations
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents alternative ways, based on the computerized systems, for the realization of protection and automation functions existing in the electric substations. The advantages and disadvantages of various solutions and the possibility of further development are analyzed.

articleTitle: Improving the Fault Location for Transmission Grids using the Existing Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the paper there are presented some results regarding the benefits of introducing the double-end location of the fault algorithms for power transmission lines. The signals of the fault were obtained with the use of a Matlab model of a 220 kV power transmission network and it was made a comparative analysis considering the distance to the failure point as parameter, which was metered from one end. After compilation the results show that the double-end fault location algorithms are more reliable when compared with the existing one-ended algorithms.

articleTitle: An approach for Improving Performance of Sensorless Field Control
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Sensorless vector control is preferred in some applications, because there is no need for speed or position sensor. However, by their very nature, they are susceptible to making position error in rotor position estimation. As a consequence the performance of motor drives employing this technology is lower than those which employ sensors. This paper presents a new approach which identifies and uses rotor slot harmonic current component in the stator current to identify rotor position. The time taken by the algorithm used is short enough to be embedded within the vector control algorithm. The essence of the algorithm is treating the current component due to rotor slot harmonics as an amplitude modulated signal on the fundamental current component. The magnitude of this current component is identified via demodulation. Using this information rotor position and speed can be determined. This approach is tested on a commercial induction motor and some results are presented which illustrate that rotor position can be successfully determined.

articleTitle: Highly Redundant Actuation System Concept with Dual Stator Six Phases BLDC Motor Suitable for Automotive Industry Applications : Fault Tolerant System Actuation Design
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Current trends in the automotive industry are geared towards the development of partially or completely autonomous drive systems. The new regulations imply increasing the security level in operation and meeting minimum requirements for fault mode assistance. In this context, the provision of redundant solutions becomes imperative. Another critical requirement is to achieve a high degree of efficiency (minimum energy consumption). This involves the development of actuation systems and specific control algorithms that increase safety, efficiency and fault tolerance behavior. Based on the abovementioned aspects, this paper proposes a study on a redundant drive concept that can be successfully integrated into the steering or brake systems of current vehicles and also fulfils the basic requirements for autonomous driving. In order to validate the theoretical aspects contained in this study, two distinct ways of modelling and simulation were used: FEM (Finite Element Method) analysis and equivalent mathematical equations implemented in MATLAB / Simulink software environment.

articleTitle: About Monitoring of Medium Voltage Circuit Breakers with SF6
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Medium voltage circuit breakers are important components on the chain of production, transmission and distribution of the energy to the consumers. The circuit breaker importance is from its capacity to make and break the currents from normal rated parameters and from short circuit currents. Over time the circuit breakers are losing them properties to break the high currents because of ageing and other electrical and mechanical stresses. From this fact is necessary to monitoring some parameters of circuit breaker. The goal of circuit breakers monitoring is to know its condition for minimize the equipment failure risk and to prevent undesirable interruptions and their effects. The paper presents the importance of a medium voltage circuit breaker with SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> in the power system, a monitoring system which was interfacing with the circuit breaker, respectively the waveforms and values obtained from its.

articleTitle: Ayrton Relation Applied for Medium Voltage AC Electrical Discharges
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to present an experimental verification of Ayrton electric arc model relation for AC medium voltage electrical discharges. In order to verify the mathematical relation, which describe the AC electrical discharge, a 10 kV and 200 mA voltage transformer having a falling volt-ampere (V - I) characteristic has been used. The discharge has been produced by a system with two copper electrodes that allows the adjustment of the distance between them and, as consequence, the adjustment of the discharge length. The electrical parameters, voltage and current, have been measured using a high voltage probe and a shunt, respectively, the corresponding waveforms being recorder with an oscilloscope and subsequently processed.

articleTitle: 98.2% Efficiency, Low Cost, 6.6-kW AC/DC Converter for HEV/EV On-Board Charger
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper examines a new structure of an AC/DC power supply for single-phase on-board chargers. The transfer of the AC power to the DC circuit is performed at high frequency (1-120 kHz). The transistors operate in a soft switching mode (ZCS) with a variable switching frequency. This reduces the switching power losses of the transistors. The charger architecture includes several identical functional modules which operate with phase shift in the input circuits. Thus, the value of the smoothing capacitor of the input filter can be reduced and also the power grid pollution with the current higher harmonics. Verification of the proposed solution was done by mathematical simulations and by testing a 1650W laboratory module prototype. The AC supply voltage can vary between 85-265V, and the DC output voltage between 250-450V. The resulted volume indicator of the converter is 4.2 kW / dm3.

articleTitle: Influence of Surface Gliding Discharges on Organic Pollutants from Aqueous Solutions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The present paper aims to assess the organic pollutants from aqueous solutions. To achieve this goal, the polluted solutions were treated with non-thermal plasma discharges. To obtain non-thermal plasma an electrical discharge gliding on the surface of the solution, was used. The surface gliding discharges reactors produce an electrical discharge in the gas phase over thin film of aqueous solution. The thin film is produced due to many small droplets of the treated solution atomized in air and argon, as carrier gases. In this manner, can be achieved an enhanced contact between treated solution and the column of discharge. To assess the pollutant removal possibility of non-thermal plasma, the decolorization of an organic water-soluble pigment (e.g. Direct Green 26) was investigated.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electrical Energy Flow in a Battery Powered Electric Vehicle, Comparing the Economical Mode and the Normal Mode under Real Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Sustainable engineering goes, according to current state of knowledge, hand in hand with products causing significantly less CO2-emissions. In consequence, in modern times, the electrification of cars becomes more and more important. There are only a few data of battery powered electric vehicles (BEVs) under real conditions. On a test bench, the New European Driving Cycle is a commonly used standard, which, however, hardly simulate actual conditions and circumstances of real drive. In order to advance R&D of the electrification of the mobility sector, data from BEVs must be generated under real conditions and the data has to be carefully analyzed. In this paper, the authors compare the driving conditions of an electric car in two different driving modes under real conditions and quantify the difference between the energy flows when driving in these two modes. These modes are: I) normal mode (no velocity limitation) and II) Economical mode (velocity limitation at 94km/h). The modes are specified by the manufacturer of the test vehicle.

Author Keywords: battery powered electric vehicle, energy flow, energy management, energy consumption, driving modes

articleTitle: Contributions to conceiving, designing, and experimenting a device for connection phase adjustment (DRFC) to a limited displacement short mobile coil motor (MBMS)
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article refers to conceiving, designing, and experimenting a synchronous switch designed to power the primary of an electrical transformer to study no load and short-circuit regime.

Author Keywords: limited displacement short mobile coil motor

articleTitle: Intelligent Sensor For An Alarm System Using ARM Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper present some of the intelligent sensor concepts and an application for object tracking, making use of data fusion concept. The ARM microcontroller processes data from two sensors: ultrasonic sensor for distance measurement and video cam. With distance and image parameters are defined normal and altered conditions. If the data conditions are altered, following rules based system, the alarm system send useful information to be displayed at the user level.

articleTitle: Energy and Thermoeconomic Analysis of Energy Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Due to environmental and demographic impacts, there is a high probability of a series of changes occurring on our planet over the next decades. In addition, a significant increase in the prices of all hydrocarbons due to limited world reserves is expected in the next decades. The combined use of renewable energy technologies and alternative energy technologies is a promising approach to reduce global warming effects in the world. In this paper, a solar concentrated power plant analysis based on the Rankine Cycle (RC) is performed, heated by means of various renewable energy sources. First, solar energy is used, followed by wood biomass energy. The solar energy is used during days full of sunshine. The heat energy from the concentrated solar power system process, stored in the big heat reservoir, is used to produce hydrogen during the night and during cloudy weather. In the period without sunshine and when we use all heat from the heat reservoir, biomass energy is used. This article examines the efficiency of a specific thermochemical hydrogen production cycle called the Copper-Chlorine cycle (CuCl). In the article, energy and economy analysis for the case of central European market prices, will be analyzed.

articleTitle: Aspects Regarding Disturbances Produced by Fluorescent Tubes
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper has a strong applicative character. There is presented a modern system for monitoring dynamic states, carried out with the help of a data acquisition board. It is insisted upon an original monitoring program conceived by the paper team. There are presented then two applications of using this system: a) (experimental) analysis of disturbances produced by a fluorescent tube; b) analysis of disturbances produced by a LED tube. A special attention is paid to the experimental aspects which emphasize the waveforms of the currents corresponding to some fluorescent tubes (in a few representative operation states). Finally, there are presented conclusions, which have been obtained by finalizing the research and the afferent bibliography.

articleTitle: OFDM based on FFT decoder with non-integer argument
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Due to its efficient use of the spectral band and also to its immunity to selective fading, Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) modulation was adopted by many of the wireless technologies of today. However resilient this modulation technique is to Inter Symbol Interference (ISI) or Inter Carrier Interference (ICI), the errors determined by this interference mechanism are significant. The present paper proposes the development of a new OFDM decoding algorithm which can demodulate data in severe ISI or ICI conditions. It is based on use of oversampling in frequency technique, performed by a Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) with non-integer argument. The obtained results are reported against the standard ones.

articleTitle: A Survey of the Magnetic Field in a MRI Area
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper we present the results of the magnetic field survey in the neighborhood of the magnetic resonance images (MRI) scanner. By using both commercial instruments and an automatic survey system realized by us, we try to study the temporal and spatial variability of the background magnetic field in a hospital area. The maximum values of the magnetic field were given in the Technical Room, namely 8289 nT, near the MRI scanner gradients panel. Although the magnetic field values are below 9% from the maximum admissible values by ICNIRP, there are many points from the Technical Room where the values exceed 0.4 μT, which carry health risk, especially for children.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Studies on Laboratory Photovoltaic Concept for Mechatronics System of Solar Electric Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents the design and construction of a laboratory off-grid photovoltaic system using analogic elements and components. Some operating subsystems are presented, such as: charging module, monitoring module for the batteries, DCDC converter, DC-AC converter. Experiments and recorded waveforms are presented and discussed. The laboratory photovoltaic system can be used for educational and researches purposes by students and researchers.

articleTitle: Laboratory Off-Grid Photovoltaic System with Two Axes Orientation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents the design and realization of a laboratory off-grid photovoltaic system with two axes orientation using analogic elements and components. The photovoltaic system is designed considering its operating subsystems, such as: modules for the horizontal orientation of the panel, modules for the vertical orientation of the panel, charging module, monitoring module for the batteries, DC-DC converter, DC-AC converter. For the main operating subsystem there are presented the design and operating mode. Experiments and a comparative analysis are considered for the next cases: the panel is fixed, the panel is oriented on a single axe, and the panel has two axes orientation. The laboratory photovoltaic system can be used for educational and researches purposes.

articleTitle: Current State of Researches in the Development of Energy Systems at Stefan cel Mare University of Suceava
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the current state of research within the Stefan cel Mare University of Suceava in the energy field. Were approached research topics in the field of Smart Grid systems, as well as researches related to the renewable energy and orientation and positioning systems of the solar panels.

articleTitle: New Solution for Impedance Protection Inter-tripping Schemes Implementation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the concepts, the way of implementation and testing of an application with significant technical and financial impact represented by the realization of tele-protection or inter-tripping distance protection schemes without using of specific additional installations. The implementation of these schemes is done by transmitting GOOSE (Generic Object-Oriented Substation Event) messages between the electrical substations belonging to the same electrical distribution or transport company.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Composites in the design of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Actuators
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents, in a comparative manner, the performances of two Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Machines (PMSM), which are used as actuators in various automotive applications. The stator of the first electric machine is based on a Vernier topology and the second has a classical structure. This paper will include an electromagnetic and thermal analysis.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the measurement uncertainty in thermoresistances calibration
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper refers to evaluation of measurement uncertainty in calibration of thermoresistances The evaluation of measurement uncertainty in the calibration of thermoresistances is necessary in order to make accurate measurements and to understand the use of measurement results. It is also important to evaluate the calibration uncertainty as part of the calibration for the purpose of mentioning it in the calibration certificate of the thermoresistance. Calibration determines the correspondence between the input and output signal of a temperature sensor. In this case, the calibration of the thermoresistance determin a dependency relationship between the input signal, electrical resistance (Ω), and the output signal, temperature (° C). A practical method for calibration thermometers with electrical resistance is using calibrators temperature or thermostatic baths, which consists of measuring the electrical resistance of the calibrated thermometer with electrical resistance, and temperature of the working medium in which the calibrated and standard thermometers are immersed, at set point temperature. All the individual uncertainty components of thermoresistance calibration should have predefined values and provide for the total extended measurement uncertainty a smaller value.

articleTitle: Method to Assess the Degradation Risk of Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the failure modes, the effects and the criticality for each element in the architecture and operation of a photovoltaic system. A typical configuration is considered: photovoltaic panel, junction box, connection cables, controller, battery and inverter. The first part of this study generally describes the current state of the failure modes and effects for each element of the photovoltaic system. In the second part of the study is presented a structured case study based on the LACARP photovoltaic system that is part of LACARP's laboratory of Faculty of Electrical Engineering of the “Gheorghe Asachi” Technical University of Iasi including customized criteria and indicators for each element of a photovoltaic system. This approach will help establishing the hierarchy and the integration of each failure mode and the level of rated power affected.

articleTitle: Trends in Scientific Research Published in International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE) Conference Series
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering celebrates this year the tenth edition. With this occasion, an analysis of papers published in the proceedings of the conference series has been carried out in order to determine the trends of the research in the field of Electrical and Power Engineering reflected by the participation in the conference. Other aspects of the conference series such as paper citations, authors' affiliation, geographical distribution of authors and collaboration with partner institutions were analyzed for determining further actions to be taken by the organizers in order to increase next editions quality, visibility, and extent. The analysis was based on the articles published in the conference proceedings from the previous nine editions.

articleTitle: Aspects of Voltage Distribution in Capacitor Batteries
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper proposes different electrical schemes of power supply which use battery of capacitors. In practice are some cases that require electronic components with specific parameters. For example, due to the very high electrical resistances of the insulating materials, to highlight the very small currents acting on them, it is necessary to use a higher voltage power supply. There is the possibility of studying different solutions to solve specific aspects into high voltage circuits. Commercially, electronic components, for a lower cost, have limited values for voltages below or close to the required supply voltage. The serial connection of the filter capacitors is a solution, but other problems arise due to the inherent differences between the capacitors' properties, even they are made with the same technologies, the same manufacturer and the same batch. Also, the possibility of design the solution for balancing or limit the voltage distribution in the supercapacitors batteries is analyzed in this paper. Due to the way accomplished technology, a nominal voltage of 2.7 or 5.5 volts of supercapacitors is the limit. Simulations and experimental of the analyzed schemes were carried out.

articleTitle: Automatic Reconfiguration of Medium Voltage Power Distribution Networks in Emergency Mode
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents a solution for automatic reconfiguration in case of emergency of medium voltage power distribution network. With these automations, a significant reduction in the amount of time needed to reconfigure the emergency networks is achieved, ranging from a few hours or even dozens of hours in extreme climatic conditions to about 20 seconds.

articleTitle: SMART CITY: Definition and Evaluation of Key Performance Indicators
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Accelerated evolution of technology and rising level of globalization have encouraged the emergence of a new concept of urban communities. Smart City model can efficiently incorporate the most recent scientific solutions in daily activities of cities, and improve living quality by integrating social resources, infrastructure modernization and economic growth. Although this novel concept is gaining more and more attention, a smart city assessment system is rarely applied in order to evaluate urban development situation, leading to unjustified decision making and unnecessary investments. In this regard, the formulation of a relevant set of key indicators is mandatory for measuring performance of cities development. The goal of the paper is to provide a comprehensive evaluation model for this system of indicators, focusing on energy and environment concerns as study subjects. With the assistance of computer programs, the z-transformation and Analytic Hierarchy Process methods are implemented for the evaluation algorithm construction. The presented model seeks to investigate the development profiles of various cities around the world, but also to carry out comparisons between performances of the selected cities.

articleTitle: Achievements and Perspectives in Contactless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The contactless transmission of electrical power has many important advantages in modern technology through the lack of electrical contacts and therefore of their ageing, the facile use in aggressive or explosive environments, in marine environments, medical applications, in electrical vehicles, in robotics. The efficiency is comparable to the galvanic contact transmission at small and medium distances but there is also the ability to simultaneously transmit energy and data. The paper makes a review of the main recent Romanian and foreign publications on the main techniques of contactless power transmission, regarding the optimization of the coupler “figure of merit”, and compensation topology, using both circuit analysis and FEM analysis. A recent application to contactless transmission via conductive fluids is discussed. Also, there are discussed the perspectives of the research, development and use of the described methods in the following years, in the scope of achieving interoperability, increasing the efficiency and the power transfer.

articleTitle: A Neuronal Model of the 3D Head Position Based on a Wearable System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Nowadays, the wearable systems start to play an increasing and very important role in the development of many applications. Their ultimate design is intended to provide final users with small, independent, low-power, wearable and unobtrusive solutions for continuous all-day and in any-place monitoring and forecast systems. The main purpose of the current paper is to present the design details, the key technologies and the practical implementation methods used in the developing of a new proposed smart clothing system able to detect, in a non-contact mode, the individual rotation of a subject head: pitch-roll-yaw. Exactly, by using four LC-based capacitive sensors embedded in a shirt collar, the CC2650 SoC, the device-to-gateway communication concept to connect to an Internet cloud service, the Bluetooth low energy standard version 4.2 in order to connect to the gateway, the TI-RTOS as a consistent embedded software platform and a neuronal network approximation model, we succeeded to successfully develop and implement a low-power wearable system, named Intell.TieSens.

articleTitle: Impact of staff competences on power quality – related ship accidents
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the threats and adequate counter - measures connected with impact of staff competences on power quality - related ship accidents. Competence gap is analyzed on the basis of the selected case studies for passenger ships and chemical tankers, and concerns the main discrepancies such as: insufficient knowledge about protection systems of critical devices for ship power plant operation as well as human errors in ship tests, day-to-day routine and periodical service and operation. The carried out analysis, is not only emphasized on the role of the human factor in ship system design, development and exploitation, but first of all is addressed to safety lessons, how to limit a hazard connected with crew member behavior in both, routine and unpredictable situations.

articleTitle: Metaheuristic Algorithms based Multi-objective Optimization for Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper a multi-threshold image segmentation procedure based on nature-inspired multi-objective optimization is proposed. The Particle Swarm Optimization, Black Hole and Gravitational Search algorithms were adapted for multi-objective optimization. The Root Mean Square Error and the number of segmented regions were used as optimization criteria. The three procedures were applied for human silhouettes detection in video sequences and the obtained results are compared. Concerning the algorithms performances, the experiments revealed that the results of multi-objective Black Hole algorithm based segmentation are better than those of the other two algorithms, at least for the test images used in this experiment.

articleTitle: Assessment of Data Center Energy Efficiency. Methods and Metrics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an assessment method for Operational Data center regarding energy efficiency. Data centers are the main part of information and communication architecture. The energy consumed in Data Centers is increasing according with the information technology and communications evolution. It can be reduced up to 40% with applying measures and strategies for energy-efficiency system management. Data centers are complex systems consisting in buildings and construction, facilities and utilities, energy and technic systems in operation. The challenge is to identify the areas that shall be improved, an objective assessment method for Operational Data Center energy efficiency is the most useful. The assessment methods and quantitative measurement for energy efficiency improvement are also important to be aligned with International Strategy in Europe and America for Energy Efficiency improvement goals to reduce the consumption in all economic sectors, including Information Technology and Communications (Data centers). Reducing data centers energy consumption is also a way to achieve energy efficiency in the buildings that host the specific facility, aligned with current standards and regulations.

articleTitle: Specific Absorption Rate Evaluation in Case of Exposure of the Human Body to Radiofrequency Electromagnetic Field Generated by Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: EMC is a permanent challenge for many items associated with radio communications. Inside this large frame work, human exposure issue should be always considered. For that, it is worth of knowing the impact on the short and on the long term of electromagnetic field irradiation over biological tissues of human body. The present paper is a study over the estimation of specific absorption rate (SAR) on a developed 3D model of the human body in case of exposure to electromagnetic fields generated by mobile communications in some areas (indoor and outdoor) with specific instrumentation (Spectran HF-60105 V4 spectrum analyzer with HyperLOG 60100 antenna). The SAR values was determined by simulation using the CST MW Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software and the values were compared with limits values for SAR imposed by ICNIRP (1998) restriction limits and European Directive 2004/40/CE standards, adopted also in Romania by HG number 1136 from 30 august 2006. Additionally, the RSAR, while dealing with simultaneous exposure to different frequency fields should be considered.

articleTitle: Primary control of inverter-based microgrids and robustness analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: We design the primary controllers of an inverter-based microgrid using pole region assignment. The lines are modeled via admittance matrix and the loads are modeled as constant impedances. Since the power demand of the loads fluctuate, we check the robustness of the closed loop against load impedance changes using the multi-model approach. While the analysis shows that the closed loop is robust against changes in the load impedances, the variations of the load impedances do not lead to the changes in power demand one would expect intuitively. Therefore, further work is necessary to research how the robustness against changes in the load demand can be investigated without the detour over the load impedances.
